home_care_measures: Immediate oral hydration: Consume 500-750 mL of water.
Rest in a quiet, dark, well-ventilated room with eyes closed for 30-45 minutes.
Apply a cold damp washcloth or ice pack (wrapped in a towel) over forehead or warm compress to posterior neck muscles.
Practice the 20-20-20 visual rest rule (look at an object 20 feet away for 20 seconds every 20 minutes of screen use).
Gentle neck and shoulder stretching to relieve myofascial tension.
medication_guidance: Acetaminophen (500-1000 mg oral every 6 hours as needed, max 3000 mg/day) ONLY IF no contraindication exists and liver function is normal. Verify with drug interaction checker before taking NSAIDs if patient takes anticoagulants or ACE inhibitors.
escalation_red_flags: Sudden 'thunderclap' onset of worst headache of life (subarachnoid hemorrhage risk)
Accompanied by neck stiffness, high fever, or photophobia (meningitis triad)
Focal neurological deficits (facial droop, unilateral limb weakness, speech slurring)
Headache on anticoagulant therapy (Warfarin, NOACs) - Mandatory Emergency Department referral
Worsening pain despite conservative measures over 48 hours

condition: Acute Viral Pharyngitis / Upper Respiratory Infection (Common Cold)
home_care_measures: Warm saline gargling: Dissolve 1/2 teaspoon of salt in 8 ounces of warm water; gargle 3-4 times daily.
Liberal oral fluid intake: Warm broths, herbal decaffeinated teas with honey, and electrolyte solutions.
Cool-mist humidifier in sleeping area to moisten inflamed respiratory mucosa.
Elevate head of bed 30 degrees during sleep to reduce post-nasal drip.
Throat lozenges containing pectin or glycerin for mucosal demulcent effect.
medication_guidance: Honey (1-2 teaspoons for cough relief in patients > 1 year old). Saline nasal spray for congestion. Antipyretic analgesics if feverish and cleared by drug checker.
escalation_red_flags: Inability to swallow saliva, drooling, or severe trismus (peritonsillar abscess / epiglottitis)
Inspiratory stridor, shortness of breath, or intercostal retractions
Persistent high fever > 39.0°C (102.2°F) refractory to antipyretics for > 72 hours
Hemoptysis (coughing up blood) or purulent sputum accompanied by pleuritic chest pain

home_care_measures: Oral Rehydration Therapy (ORT): Small, frequent sips (5-10 mL every 5 minutes) of oral rehydration salts (ORS), dilute broths, or electrolyte solutions.
Temporary gut rest: Avoid dairy, fatty foods, high-sugar beverages, alcohol, and caffeine for 24-48 hours.
Gradual dietary reintroduction: BRAT diet (Bananas, Rice, Applesauce, Toast) once vomiting has subsided for > 6 hours.
Strict hand hygiene with soap and water to limit enterovirus/norovirus transmission.
medication_guidance: Avoid antimotility agents (Loperamide) if high fever or bloody stools are present. Review all chronic medications (especially diuretics, ACE inhibitors, and Metformin) to prevent hypovolemia-induced renal injury.
escalation_red_flags: Signs of severe dehydration: Anuria (no urination > 8 hours), sunken eyes, dry mucous membranes, postural syncope
Hematemesis (coffee-ground emesis) or frank hematochezia (bloody stools)
Severe localized abdominal rigidity or peritoneal rebound tenderness
Intractable vomiting preventing oral fluid intake for > 12 hours

home_care_measures: Allergen avoidance: Keep windows closed during high pollen counts; shower and change clothes after outdoor exposure.
Nasal saline irrigation (Neti pot) with distilled or sterile saline twice daily.
Cold compress over eyes to soothe allergic conjunctival pruritus.
medication_guidance: Intranasal corticosteroid spray (Fluticasone) or non-sedating second-generation oral antihistamine (Cetirizine, Loratadine). Verify patient does not take medications that prolong QTc or interact with antihistamines.
escalation_red_flags: Facial, lip, or tongue angioedema
Wheezing, chest tightness, or respiratory compromise (Anaphylaxis risk - Call EMS / 911)
Unilateral foul-smelling nasal discharge with facial pressure (bacterial sinusitis / obstruction)

condition: Acute Lumbosacral Muscle Strain (Mild Back Strain)
home_care_measures: Avoid prolonged complete bed rest; maintain gentle, pain-free active movement and short walks.
Apply ice pack wrapped in cloth for 15-20 minutes every 2-3 hours during the initial 48 hours; transition to moist heat thereafter.
Sleeping posture: Side sleeping with pillow between knees or back sleeping with pillow under knees to reduce lumbar lordotic stress.
Ergonomic lumbar support while sitting.
medication_guidance: Topical menthol or lidocaine patches. Oral analgesics if cleared by drug interaction checker (caution with NSAIDs in renal disease, hypertension, or anticoagulation).
escalation_red_flags: Cauda Equina Syndrome: Sudden loss of bowel or bladder sphincter control, saddle anesthesia (loss of sensation in perineum/buttocks)
Progressive lower extremity neurological deficit (foot drop, loss of leg motor power)
History of malignancy or unexplained weight loss
Back pain accompanied by unexplained high fever
